title: Technical (Risk Assurance) – Test 8: Mixed Mock Exam

questions.text: An auditor is deciding which systems are in scope for ITGC testing in a financial statement audit. Which is most likely in scope?

options.A: The staff canteen's meal ordering app on phones
options.B: The meeting room booking system at head office
options.C: The ERP that records sales and posts to the ledger
options.D: The company's public marketing website on the internet

questions.explanation: ITGCs are tested for systems that support financial reporting, where a failure could affect the figures. A public website matters for cybersecurity, but it doesn't process the company's accounting.

questions.text: A company uses a SaaS ERP whose vendor releases updates every month. What change-management control is still expected at the company?

options.A: Leave it to the vendor, which is responsible for ERP changes
options.B: Review the release notes and test the impact on key processes
options.C: Block vendor updates permanently to keep the ERP stable and unchanged
options.D: Approve each line of the vendor's source code before release

questions.explanation: The vendor controls its code, but the customer must understand how updates affect its configuration, reports and controls. "The vendor is responsible" is tempting, but it ignores the customer's side of the shared model.

questions.text: Attackers logged in to a company's VPN using an employee's stolen password. Which control would most directly have stopped this?

options.A: Annual security awareness training for staff
options.B: Encrypting laptop hard drives
options.C: A longer password expiry period
options.D: Multi-factor authentication on the VPN

questions.explanation: With MFA, a stolen password alone isn't enough to log in. Awareness training might have reduced the chance of the password being stolen, but it wouldn't stop the login once it was.

questions.text: A software company that builds its own applications excludes the Annex A control on secure development from its Statement of Applicability, giving no reason. What should the ISO/IEC 27001 auditor conclude?

options.A: Acceptable, as Annex A is guidance that certified firms may set aside
options.B: Acceptable, as any Annex A control may be excluded without explanation
options.C: A nonconformity: the exclusion is unjustified and doesn't fit the risks
options.D: Acceptable while no incident has been caused by the exclusion

questions.explanation: The Statement of Applicability must justify every exclusion, and an exclusion must follow from the risk assessment. A developer excluding secure development with no reason fails both. Annex A isn't optional guidance: its controls must be compared with the ones chosen.

questions.text: After an outage, the team restores systems from backups, confirms they work and updates stakeholders on progress. Which NIST CSF 2.0 function is this?

options.A: Respond
options.B: Identify
options.C: Recover
options.D: Protect

questions.explanation: Recover covers restoring assets and operations and communicating about recovery. Respond is tempting, but it covers managing and containing the incident itself, not restoring normal operations.

questions.text: In a phishing simulation, 30% of staff clicked the test link. What is the most appropriate response?

options.A: Stop the simulations, since the results were so poor
options.B: Block incoming external email for the whole company
options.C: Formal disciplinary action for every employee who clicked
options.D: Targeted awareness training plus stronger email filtering

questions.explanation: People and technical controls work together: training for those who clicked, filtering to cut how many phishing emails arrive. Disciplining everyone is tempting as a firm response but discourages reporting.

questions.text: A company requires two signatures on every payment above a set limit. Which COSO component does this belong to?

options.A: Control activities
options.B: Monitoring activities
options.C: Control environment
options.D: Risk assessment

questions.explanation: Dual authorisation is a control activity: an action set by policy to reduce a risk. Monitoring would be a later check that the dual-signature rule is actually followed.

questions.text: In the IIA Three Lines Model, who is accountable to stakeholders for oversight of the organisation?

options.A: The external auditor
options.B: Internal audit
options.C: Management
options.D: The governing body

questions.explanation: The governing body (e.g. the board) is accountable to stakeholders for oversight. Internal audit is tempting because it reports to the board, but it provides assurance and advice; it doesn't own oversight.

questions.text: A key review control failed testing, but a separate control that detects the same misstatements was tested and found effective. How does this affect the evaluation?

options.A: The failed control is no longer treated as a deficiency
options.B: The compensating control has to be ignored in the evaluation
options.C: The compensating control may reduce how severe the deficiency is
options.D: Both controls now have to be reported as material weaknesses

questions.explanation: Compensating controls are considered when judging the severity of a deficiency, but the deficiency itself remains and is still reported at the right level. Saying it disappears is the tempting mistake.

questions.text: What is the main limitation of observation as audit evidence?

options.A: It is less reliable than just asking the staff member about it
options.B: It shows only that the control ran while being watched
options.C: It can't be written up in the audit working papers
options.D: It isn't accepted as evidence for IT controls

questions.explanation: Observation is good evidence at that moment, but people may act differently when watched, and it says nothing about the rest of the period. It is more reliable than inquiry, not less.

questions.text: A retailer collected customers' phone numbers to arrange deliveries and now wants to use them for marketing messages. Under UU PDP, what is needed?

options.A: A valid basis for the new purpose, e.g. explicit consent
options.B: Deleting the numbers, as phone numbers can't be stored
options.C: Just a limit of one marketing message a month
options.D: No new step, since the retailer already holds the numbers

questions.explanation: UU PDP requires processing to be limited to specific purposes and to have a lawful basis (Articles 16 and 20). A new purpose needs its own basis, typically consent for marketing. Already holding the data is not a basis.

questions.text: A customer asks a company to erase their personal data. No law requires the company to keep it and there is no legal dispute. What should the company do?

options.A: Keep the data indefinitely for future analytics projects
options.B: Refuse the request, because consent was given earlier
options.C: Erase the customer's name but keep the other fields
options.D: Erase the data and inform the customer that it was erased

questions.explanation: Data subjects may ask for erasure, and the controller must erase or destroy the data and tell the subject it has done so (Articles 8, 43–45). Earlier consent doesn't block this, since consent can be withdrawn.

questions.text: Before moving its accounting system to a cloud provider, which document best gives the company independent assurance over the provider's controls?

options.A: A recent SOC 1 or SOC 2 Type 2 report on the service
options.B: The provider's marketing brochure about its security
options.C: The provider's own self-assessment questionnaire
options.D: A reference call with one of the provider's customers

questions.explanation: A Type 2 SOC report is an independent auditor's opinion on controls tested over a period. A self-assessment is tempting because it is detailed, but it is written by the provider itself.

questions.text: Which SOC report is meant for general use and can be published, e.g. on the provider's website?

options.A: SOC 3
options.B: SOC 1 Type 1
options.C: SOC 1 Type 2
options.D: SOC 2 Type 2

questions.explanation: SOC 3 is a short general-use report on the trust services criteria. SOC 2 Type 2 covers the same criteria in detail, which is why it is tempting, but its use is restricted to people who understand the system.

questions.text: A disaster recovery test restored the ERP at the backup site in 10 hours. The ERP's recovery time objective (RTO) is 4 hours. The IT manager records the test as "passed" because the system came back. What should the auditor conclude?

options.A: The test missed its RTO; the gap needs a remediation plan
options.B: The test failed its recovery point objective, not the RTO
options.C: The test passed, because the system was fully recovered
options.D: The RTO should simply be changed to 10 hours to match

questions.explanation: The RTO is the target the test measures, so 10 hours against 4 means the plan doesn't meet business needs. Raising the RTO is tempting, but the RTO comes from the business impact analysis; it can't be changed to fit a test result.

questions.text: Your key cloud vendor uses a subcontractor to run its data centres. What should your vendor due diligence cover?

options.A: The subcontractor's marketing and brand policies
options.B: How the vendor oversees its own subcontractors
options.C: No review, as you have no contract with the subcontractor
options.D: The subcontractor's prices for its services

questions.explanation: Risk flows through the supply chain, so due diligence covers how the vendor manages its fourth parties. Having no direct contract is tempting as a reason to stop, but the data is still exposed there.

questions.text: In journal entry testing, which entries would an auditor usually treat as higher risk?

options.A: Entries created automatically by the billing interface
options.B: Entries that are matched to approved purchase orders
options.C: Recurring monthly depreciation entries set up by the finance team
options.D: Manual entries posted at unusual times or by unusual users

questions.explanation: Fraud through management override often shows up as manual entries at odd times, by unexpected users, with round amounts or odd accounts. Automated interface entries are routine and covered by other controls.

questions.text: Most employees have local administrator rights on their company laptops. What is the main risk?

options.A: The laptops will need to be backed up more often than other laptops
options.B: Users can install software, including malware, and turn off security
options.C: Users are more likely to forget the password for their own laptop
options.D: The network will become slower for other users across the company

questions.explanation: Admin rights let users (and any malware running as them) install programs and disable protection. Backups and network speed aren't affected by who is an administrator.

questions.text: Which control protects data sent between a user's browser and a web application?

options.A: Full-disk encryption
options.B: Account lockout
options.C: TLS (HTTPS)
options.D: Database backups

questions.explanation: TLS encrypts data in transit between browser and server. Full-disk encryption is tempting as "encryption", but it protects data at rest on a device.

questions.text: The customer master file has many duplicate customers, created by different branches for the same person. Which control best prevents new duplicates?

options.A: A once-a-year clean-up by IT without any business input
options.B: A system duplicate check when a new customer is created
options.C: Encrypting the customer master file on the database
options.D: Letting each branch keep its own separate customer list

questions.explanation: A check at the point of entry stops duplicates before they exist (preventive). A yearly clean-up is tempting but detective and after the fact, and without the business it can merge the wrong records.
